sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

## RWX PR previews

`.rwx/preview.yml` defines the preview app (see the `rwx-reflex-preview` skill in
`.agents/skills/`). Validate with `rwx lint .rwx/preview.yml`; test with
`rwx run .rwx/preview.yml --init pull-request-number=0 --wait`. Previews are
private: access them with the `X-RWX-Access-Token` header (RWX docs). Only use
behavior documented in the RWX docs or `rwx --help`. Known open issue: the
frontend's baked-in `localhost:8000` API URL is patched in the build step
(undocumented workaround, WebSocket events unverified).

## Build & Test

```bash
uv sync --group dev          # install locked deps into .venv
uv run pytest -q             # smoke tests (`network`-marked tests deselected)
uv run tach check            # module boundaries
uv run tach check-external   # declared vs imported dependencies
uv run python scripts/check_frontend.py  # JS deps vs reflex.lock (needs bun; ~1 min)
trunk check --all            # lint (run uv sync first: pyright/pyrefly use .venv)
```

## Conventions

- Layers are `web.web` -> `web.pages.*` -> `web.components.*`, enforced by
  `tach.toml`; new modules need an explicit entry there.
- `tach check-external` is its own task in `.rwx/trunk-check.yml`, not a Trunk
  linter: Trunk lints from a sandbox holding only the diff, which makes every
  dependency look unused.
- `uv` ignores packages published in the last 7 days (`[tool.uv] exclude-newer`);
  pyrefly/pyright/tach pins must match between `pyproject.toml` and
  `.trunk/trunk.yaml`.
- RWX: a green run is not proof a step worked. Read task logs (`rwx logs`) for
  steps that talk to third parties.
- Use non-interactive flags (`-y`, `-f`, `trunk ... --ci < /dev/null`) in
  scripted commands.

## Git workflow

- Commit only when the user explicitly asks; show what will be committed first.
- Do not push to the remote unless explicitly asked.
- Ask before using any escape hatch that bypasses a check (skip flags,
  `--no-verify`, lint/type ignores).

</project_instructions>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. A tool whose declaration returns an object resolves on failure too when it returned that object; check its fields. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /Users/elvis/.npm/_npx/99fca8174466655b/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

# Pool Worker

You are a pool worker agent in a Gas City workspace. You were spawned
because work is available. Find it, execute it, close it, and exit.

Your agent name is `$GC_AGENT`. Your session ID is `$GC_SESSION_ID`.

## GUPP — If you find work, YOU RUN IT.

No confirmation, no waiting. You were spawned with work. Run it.
When you're done, exit. The reconciler will spawn a new worker when
more work arrives.

## Startup Protocol

Find and claim your work with the hook. This is the one command — do not
substitute a `gc bd list` or `gc bd ready` query of your own:

```bash
# Finds existing assigned work, assigned ready work, or atomically claims
# routed work. If nothing is available, it acknowledges runtime drain.
gc hook --claim --drain-ack --json
```

If the result action is `work`, read the returned `bead_id` with
`gc bd show <id>`. If the result action is `drain`, the drain was
acknowledged for you: your session is done — exit.

**Never look for your work with `gc bd list --assignee=<your alias>` or
`gc bd ready`.** Pool work is invisible to those queries twice over: an
unclaimed routed item has NO assignee, and it is an ephemeral wisp, which
`gc bd list` and `gc bd ready` hide by default. A worker that checks that way
reports "no work" while its own wisp sits open — that is how a scheduled
maintenance order once went 41 hours without running (ga-tmzjx6). Claiming
does not rescue such a query either: a claim is recorded under the session
identity the SDK exported, not the alias you would guess, so on resume it is
equally invisible.

There is no shorter query to fall back to. The work lookup your config
resolves to is several hundred characters of shell and jq — it walks session
ID, session name and alias, then falls through to pool demand, and it handles
the ephemeral-wisp cases that plain `bd` subcommands miss. `gc hook` exists so
that you never have to reproduce it. If the hook is failing, report that as a
fault; do not work around it with a query you composed yourself.

## Following Your Formula

Your formula defines your work as a sequence of steps. Steps are NOT
materialized as individual beads — they exist in the formula definition.
Read the step descriptions and work through them in order.

**THE RULE**: Execute one step at a time. Verify completion. Move to next.
Do NOT skip ahead. Do NOT claim steps done without actually doing them.

On crash or restart, re-read your formula steps and determine where you
left off from context (last completed action, git state, bead state).

**Never use wide filesystem searches when a CLI command exists.** Wide
traversals (`find /`, `find ~`, `find /Users`, `find $HOME`) walk
TCC-protected directories on macOS — Documents, Desktop, Downloads,
removable volumes — and trigger permission prompts that block work. If
you don't know how to locate a formula, recipe, bead, mail, or Dolt
state, the answer is a `gc` introspection command, not a
filesystem search. If no command exists for what you need, file a bead.

## Molecules — STOP, check BEFORE you start working

**CRITICAL:** When you run `gc bd show` in step 4, look at the METADATA
section. If it contains `molecule_id`, your work is governed by that
molecule's steps. Do NOT just read the description and start coding.

Run `gc bd mol current <molecule-id>` to see your steps:

- `[done]` — step is complete
- `[current]` — step is in progress (you are here)
- `[ready]` — step is ready to start
- `[blocked]` — step is waiting on dependencies

**Work one step at a time.** For each `[ready]` step:
1. `gc bd show <step-id>` — read what to do
2. Do the work described in that step
3. `gc bd close <step-id>` — mark it done
4. `gc bd mol current <molecule-id>` — check your position, repeat

Do NOT read the parent bead description and do everything at once.
Do NOT skip steps. Do NOT close steps you didn't execute.

If there is no `molecule_id` in the metadata, execute the work from
the bead description directly.

## Your Tools

- `gc hook --claim --json` — find and atomically claim work
- `gc bd show <id>` — see details of a work item or step
- `gc bd mol current <molecule-id>` — show position in molecule workflow
- `gc bd mol progress <molecule-id>` — show molecule progress summary
- `gc bd close <id>` — mark work or a step as done
- `gc mail inbox` — check for messages
- `gc runtime drain-ack` — end your session (you are ephemeral)

## How to Work

1. Find and claim work: `gc hook --claim --drain-ack --json`
2. If the action is `drain`, exit. If the action is `work`, read `bead_id`.
3. **Check for molecule:** `gc bd show <id>` — look for `molecule_id` in METADATA
4. **If molecule exists:** `gc bd mol current <mol-id>` → work each step in order (show → do → close → repeat)
5. **If no molecule:** execute the work directly from the bead description
6. When all work is done, close the bead: `gc bd close <id>`
7. **MANDATORY — run this exact command as your final action:**
   ```bash
   gc runtime drain-ack
   ```
   You MUST run `gc runtime drain-ack` after closing the bead. This is
   not optional. Without it, you will block other work from being picked
   up. Do NOT say "drained" without actually running the command. Do NOT
   output any text after running it.

## Escalation

When blocked, escalate — do not wait silently. `human` is the reserved
recipient alias that resolves in every city; if your city staffs a
coordinator role (e.g. the gastown pack's mayor), mail that instead:

```bash
gc mail send human -s "BLOCKED: Brief description" -m "Details of the issue"
```

## Context Exhaustion

If your context is filling up during long work:

```bash
gc runtime request-restart
```

This blocks until the controller restarts your session. The new session
picks up where you left off — find your work bead and molecule position.


## Skills available to this session

You are `cmu-database-group-lectures/pi-1`. The following skills are materialized in your provider's skill directory and load automatically — you don't need to invoke anything extra.

### Shared in this scope

- `core.gc-agents` — Managing agents — list, peek, nudge, suspend, drain *(core)*
- `core.gc-city` — City lifecycle — status, start, stop, init *(core)*
- `core.gc-dashboard` — API server and web dashboard — config, start, monitor *(core)*
- `core.gc-dispatch` — Routing work to agents with gc sling and formulas *(core)*
- `core.gc-mail` — Sending and reading messages between agents *(core)*
- `core.gc-rigs` — Managing rigs — add, list, status, suspend, resume *(core)*
- `core.gc-work` — Finding, creating, claiming, and closing work items (beads) *(core)*
- `gascity.mayor` — Coordinate requirements, implementation plans, bead creation, and formula workflow launches for a Gas City rig. Use this whenever the user references the Mayor by name or handle, including Mayor, mayor, $mayor, /mayor, @mayor, or asks the Mayor to plan, create beads, schedule, start, or run a workflow. *(gascity)*

These are discovery-time hints, not execution gates — the vendor loads every skill from the sink directory regardless of what this appendix lists.

"""Modal search API for the CMU Database Group lecture corpus (cdgl-99e).

The public notebook never touches LanceDB: LanceDB Cloud has no read-only
API keys (docs/lancedb-findings.md), so this Modal app ('cmu-lecture-search')
holds the key as a Modal secret and answers read-only search requests.

**Embedding is client-side by design:** the caller (the molab notebook)
embeds the query itself — Nomic v1.5 with the ``search_query: `` prefix, on
a molab GPU if available else CPU, via ``lecture_search.embed.embed_query``
— and sends the vector in the request. The Modal image therefore carries
only ``lancedb`` + ``fastapi``: no sentence-transformers/transformers/
einops/torch and no baked model weights, so the image is small, cold starts
are fast, and no CPU time is billed for embedding.

Endpoints (FastAPI, served via ``modal.asgi_app``):

- ``POST /search`` — hybrid search (vector + FTS, MRR reranker, same
  construction as ``notebooks/search.py``). Body:
  ``{query, vector, top_k, fts_weight, date_from?, date_to?, video_ids?}``
  where ``query`` is the raw text (used for the FTS half) and ``vector`` is
  the client-embedded query (exactly 768 finite floats).
  Returns ``{"results": [...]}`` with rows containing only
  ``video_id, title, date, start_seconds, end_seconds, deep_link, text,
  score`` — never vectors, keys, URIs or stack traces.
- ``GET /lectures`` — ``{"lectures": [{video_id, title, date}]}`` for the
  notebook's lecture filter (cached per container).

Security posture: the endpoint is public and unauthenticated, so every
input is validated hard (see ``parse_search_request``) and WHERE clauses are
only ever built from values that survived that validation
(``build_where``). The request body is size-capped (``check_body_size``)
before it is parsed.

Deploy (never prints secrets)::

    MODAL_PROFILE=marcella modal deploy lecture_search/search_api.py

Config comes from the Modal secret ``lancedb-search`` (LANCEDB_URI,
LANCEDB_API_KEY, LANCEDB_REGION, LANCEDB_TABLE); see docs/search-api.md.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
import os
import re
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from typing import Protocol

import lancedb
from lancedb.rerankers import MRRReranker, Reranker

# Deploy-only dependencies: baked into the Modal image below, intentionally
# absent from the dev venv, so the pure request/response logic stays
# importable (and testable) without them. The two guards are separate on
# purpose: the local `modal deploy` process has modal but NOT fastapi (the
# FastAPI names are only touched inside `web()`, which runs in-container).
try:
    import modal
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - local dev has no modal installed
    modal = None  # type: ignore[assignment]

try:
    from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
    from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
    from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - only the Modal image has fastapi
    FastAPI = Request = CORSMiddleware = JSONResponse = None  # type: ignore[assignment]

APP_NAME = "cmu-lecture-search"
DEFAULT_TABLE = "lectures"
DEFAULT_REGION = "us-east-1"

# Nomic v1.5 embedding dimension. Duplicated from lecture_search.embed on
# purpose: importing lecture_search.embed here would pull sentence-
# transformers into the container, defeating the client-side-embedding
# design (the image must stay lancedb + fastapi only).
VECTOR_DIMS = 768

# Hard request limits (public, unauthenticated, read-only endpoint).
# A legitimate body is dominated by the 768-float vector (~15 KB as JSON),
# so 20 KB caps it with headroom and rejects vector-padded payloads.
MAX_BODY_BYTES = 20 * 1024
MAX_QUERY_CHARS = 300
MAX_TOP_K = 50
DEFAULT_TOP_K = 10
DEFAULT_FTS_WEIGHT = 0.5
MAX_VIDEO_IDS = 50
VIDEO_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{11}$")

# Container shape: small CPU service, aggressive limits, fast scale-down.
MAX_CONTAINERS = 5
MAX_CONCURRENT_INPUTS = 8
SCALEDOWN_WINDOW_SECONDS = 300
LECTURES_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 3600
# Upper bound on rows scanned to build the distinct lecture list.
LECTURE_SCAN_LIMIT = 200_000
# LanceDB Cloud rejects empty-search scans with k > 10000 ("k cannot be
# bigger than 10000"), so the /lectures scan pages with offset() at this
# page size instead of issuing one LECTURE_SCAN_LIMIT-row query.
LECTURE_SCAN_PAGE_SIZE = 10_000


class QueryBuilder(Protocol):
    """The slice of the LanceDB query builder this service composes."""

    def vector(self, vector: list[float]) -> QueryBuilder:
        """Set the query vector."""
        ...

    def text(self, text: str) -> QueryBuilder:
        """Set the FTS query text."""
        ...

    def rerank(self, reranker: Reranker) -> QueryBuilder:
        """Set the reranker."""
        ...

    def limit(self, limit: int) -> QueryBuilder:
        """Set the result limit."""
        ...

    def offset(self, offset: int) -> QueryBuilder:
        """Skip the first ``offset`` rows (scan pagination)."""
        ...

    def where(self, where: str) -> QueryBuilder:
        """Set a SQL WHERE clause."""
        ...

    def select(self, columns: list[str]) -> QueryBuilder:
        """Project the given columns."""
        ...

    def to_list(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
        """Materialize results as a list of row dicts."""
        ...


class SearchTable(Protocol):
    """The slice of a LanceDB table this service uses (read-only)."""

    def search(self, query_type: str = "auto") -> QueryBuilder:
        """Start a search (or, with no query, a scan)."""
        ...


class RequestValidationError(ValueError):
    """A /search payload failed validation; maps to HTTP 422.

    Messages are generic on purpose: they describe the rule that was
    violated, never echo the offending input back.
    """


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SearchParams:
    """Validated, safe-to-use /search parameters."""

    query: str
    vector: tuple[float, ...]
    top_k: int
    fts_weight: float
    date_from: date | None
    date_to: date | None
    video_ids: tuple[str, ...]


def check_body_size(body: bytes) -> None:
    """Reject oversized request bodies before parsing (see MAX_BODY_BYTES)."""
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        msg = f"request body must be at most {MAX_BODY_BYTES} bytes"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg)


def _parse_vector(value: object) -> tuple[float, ...]:
    if not isinstance(value, list) or len(value) != VECTOR_DIMS:
        msg = f"vector must be a list of exactly {VECTOR_DIMS} numbers"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg)
    components: list[float] = []
    for component in value:
        if isinstance(component, bool) or not isinstance(component, (int, float)):
            msg = "vector components must be numbers"
            raise RequestValidationError(msg)
        number = float(component)
        if not math.isfinite(number):
            msg = "vector components must be finite (no NaN or infinity)"
            raise RequestValidationError(msg)
        components.append(number)
    return tuple(components)


def _parse_optional_date(value: object, field: str) -> date | None:
    if value is None:
        return None
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        msg = f"{field} must be an ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD)"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg)
    try:
        return date.fromisoformat(value)
    except ValueError:
        msg = f"{field} must be an ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD)"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg) from None


def _parse_top_k(value: object) -> int:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
        msg = f"top_k must be an integer between 1 and {MAX_TOP_K}"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg)
    if not 1 <= value <= MAX_TOP_K:
        msg = f"top_k must be an integer between 1 and {MAX_TOP_K}"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg)
    return value


def _parse_fts_weight(value: object) -> float:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        msg = "fts_weight must be a number between 0 and 1"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg)
    weight = float(value)
    if not 0.0 <= weight <= 1.0:
        msg = "fts_weight must be a number between 0 and 1"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg)
    return weight


def _parse_video_ids(value: object) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    if value is None:
        return ()
    if not isinstance(value, list) or len(value) > MAX_VIDEO_IDS:
        msg = f"video_ids must be a list of at most {MAX_VIDEO_IDS} video IDs"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg)
    if any(
        not isinstance(video_id, str) or not VIDEO_ID_RE.fullmatch(video_id)
        for video_id in value
    ):
        msg = "video_ids must be 11-character YouTube video IDs"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg)
    return tuple(value)


def parse_search_request(payload: object) -> SearchParams:
    """Validate a raw JSON body into typed, safe-to-use SearchParams.

    Every field that can end up in a WHERE clause or a LanceDB call is
    constrained here: dates become ``datetime.date`` (only ever rendered via
    ``isoformat()``) and video_ids must match a strict regex, so nothing a
    user sends can be interpreted as SQL. The query vector is validated for
    shape and finiteness but is never interpreted as text.
    """
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        msg = "request body must be a JSON object"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg)

    query = payload.get("query")
    if not isinstance(query, str) or not query.strip():
        msg = "query must be a non-empty string"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg)
    if len(query) > MAX_QUERY_CHARS:
        msg = f"query must be at most {MAX_QUERY_CHARS} characters"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg)

    date_from = _parse_optional_date(payload.get("date_from"), "date_from")
    date_to = _parse_optional_date(payload.get("date_to"), "date_to")
    if date_from is not None and date_to is not None and date_from > date_to:
        msg = "date_from must not be after date_to"
        raise RequestValidationError(msg)

    return SearchParams(
        query=query,
        vector=_parse_vector(payload.get("vector")),
        top_k=_parse_top_k(payload.get("top_k", DEFAULT_TOP_K)),
        fts_weight=_parse_fts_weight(payload.get("fts_weight", DEFAULT_FTS_WEIGHT)),
        date_from=date_from,
        date_to=date_to,
        video_ids=_parse_video_ids(payload.get("video_ids")),
    )


def build_where(params: SearchParams) -> str | None:
    """Build a WHERE clause from validated params only.

    ``date`` values come from ``datetime.date.isoformat()`` and video IDs
    have already matched ``^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{11}$``, so interpolated values can
    never break out of their string literals. Raw user input is never
    interpolated.
    """
    clauses: list[str] = []
    if params.date_from is not None:
        clauses.append(f"date >= '{params.date_from.isoformat()}'")
    if params.date_to is not None:
        clauses.append(f"date <= '{params.date_to.isoformat()}'")
    if params.video_ids:
        quoted = ", ".join(f"'{video_id}'" for video_id in params.video_ids)
        clauses.append(f"video_id IN ({quoted})")
    return " AND ".join(clauses) if clauses else None


def serialize_row(row: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Whitelist one result row: no vector, no internal columns, no keys."""
    score = row.get("_relevance_score")
    return {
        "video_id": str(row["video_id"]),
        "title": str(row["title"]),
        "date": str(row["date"]),
        "start_seconds": float(row["start_seconds"]),
        "end_seconds": float(row["end_seconds"]),
        "deep_link": str(row["deep_link"]),
        "text": str(row["text"]),
        "score": float(score) if score is not None else None,
    }


def run_hybrid_search(
    table: SearchTable,
    params: SearchParams,
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Run the same hybrid search as notebooks/search.py, then serialize.

    The query vector arrives pre-embedded by the caller; this service never
    runs an embedding model.
    """
    builder = (
        table.search(query_type="hybrid")
        .vector(list(params.vector))
        .text(params.query)
        .rerank(
            MRRReranker(
                weight_vector=1.0 - params.fts_weight,
                weight_fts=params.fts_weight,
            ),
        )
        .limit(params.top_k)
    )
    where = build_where(params)
    if where is not None:
        builder = builder.where(where)
    return [serialize_row(row) for row in builder.to_list()]


def scan_lecture_rows(
    table: SearchTable,
    page_size: int = LECTURE_SCAN_PAGE_SIZE,
    scan_limit: int = LECTURE_SCAN_LIMIT,
) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Scan up to ``scan_limit`` chunk rows for the lecture list.

    LanceDB Cloud's RemoteTable has no ``.query()``; an empty ``.search()``
    with select/limit acts as a full-table scan, but the cloud service caps
    a single scan at 10000 rows, so this pages with ``offset()`` until a
    short page or ``scan_limit`` is reached.
    """
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    offset = 0
    while offset < scan_limit:
        page_limit = min(page_size, scan_limit - offset)
        page = (
            table.search()
            .select(["video_id", "title", "date"])
            .limit(page_limit)
            .offset(offset)
            .to_list()
        )
        rows.extend(page)
        if len(page) < page_limit:
            break
        offset += page_limit
    return rows


def summarize_lectures(rows: list[dict[str, object]]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Dedupe scanned chunk rows into one {video_id, title, date} per lecture."""
    lectures: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
    for row in rows:
        video_id = str(row["video_id"])
        if video_id not in lectures:
            lectures[video_id] = {
                "video_id": video_id,
                "title": str(row["title"]),
                "date": str(row["date"]),
            }
    return sorted(
        lectures.values(),
        key=lambda lecture: (lecture["date"], lecture["title"]),
        reverse=True,
    )


if modal is not None:
    app = modal.App(APP_NAME)

    # Slim image: no embedding model, no torch, no baked weights — the
    # caller embeds. lancedb + fastapi only, so builds and cold starts are
    # fast and cheap.
    image = (
        modal.Image.debian_slim(python_version="3.12")
        .pip_install(
            "lancedb==0.40.0",
            "fastapi>=0.115,<1",
        )
        .add_local_python_source("lecture_search")
    )

    @app.cls(
        image=image,
        secrets=[modal.Secret.from_name("lancedb-search")],
        cpu=1.0,
        memory=1024,
        REDACTED,
        scaledown_window=SCALEDOWN_WINDOW_SECONDS,
    )
    @modal.concurrent(max_inputs=MAX_CONCURRENT_INPUTS)
    class SearchService:
        """CPU container: LanceDB connection, opened once (no model)."""

        table: SearchTable
        _lectures_cache: tuple[float, list[dict[str, str]]] | None

        @modal.enter()
        def load(self) -> None:
            """Connect to LanceDB once per container.

            Config arrives via the ``lancedb-search`` Modal secret.
            """
            db = lancedb.connect(
                os.environ["LANCEDB_URI"],
                region=os.environ.get("LANCEDB_REGION", DEFAULT_REGION),
                api_key=REDACTED,
            )
            table_name = os.environ.get("LANCEDB_TABLE", DEFAULT_TABLE)
            self.table = db.open_table(table_name)  # type: ignore[assignment]
            self._lectures_cache = None

        def _lectures(self) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
            now = time.time()
            cache = self._lectures_cache
            ttl = LECTURES_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS
            if cache is not None and now - cache[0] < ttl:
                return cache[1]
            rows = scan_lecture_rows(self.table)
            lectures = summarize_lectures(rows)
            self._lectures_cache = (now, lectures)
            return lectures

        @modal.asgi_app()
        def web(self) -> FastAPI:
            """Build the read-only FastAPI app (CORS allow-all, no docs)."""
            api = FastAPI(
                title=APP_NAME,
                docs_url=None,
                redoc_url=None,
                openapi_url=None,
            )
            # Read-only public API; CORS allow-all is fine.
            api.add_middleware(
                CORSMiddleware,
                allow_origins=["*"],
                allow_methods=["GET", "POST"],
                allow_headers=["*"],
            )

            @api.post("/search", response_model=None)
            async def search(
                request: Request,
            ) -> JSONResponse | dict[str, list[dict[str, object]]]:
                # Read the raw body first so the size cap applies before any
                # JSON parsing work happens.
                body = await request.body()
                try:
                    check_body_size(body)
                except RequestValidationError as exc:
                    return JSONResponse(status_code=422, content={"error": str(exc)})
                try:
                    payload: object = json.loads(body)
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    return JSONResponse(
                        status_code=422,
                        content={"error": "request body must be valid JSON"},
                    )
                try:
                    params = parse_search_request(payload)
                except RequestValidationError as exc:
                    return JSONResponse(status_code=422, content={"error": str(exc)})
                # Broad-but-enumerated catch: LanceDB and I/O failures all
                # map to a generic 500. Anything else propagates to FastAPI's
                # ServerErrorMiddleware, which returns a bare "Internal
                # Server Error" — still no stack trace or internals.
                try:
                    rows = run_hybrid_search(self.table, params)
                except (ValueError, RuntimeError, OSError, KeyError, TypeError):
                    return JSONResponse(
                        status_code=500,
                        content={"error": "search failed"},
                    )
                return {"results": rows}

            @api.get("/lectures", response_model=None)
            def lectures() -> JSONResponse | dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]]:
                try:
                    return {"lectures": self._lectures()}
                except (ValueError, RuntimeError, OSError, KeyError, TypeError):
                    return JSONResponse(
                        status_code=500,
                        content={"error": "failed to list lectures"},
                    )

            return api

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Protocol

import lancedb
from lancedb.embeddings import get_registry
from lancedb.pydantic import LanceModel, Vector

NOMIC_MODEL = "nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5"
EMBEDDING_DIMS = 768
DOCUMENT_PREFIX = "search_document: "
QUERY_PREFIX = "search_query: "

# Registry embedder instantiated ONCE at module import. Instantiating is
# cheap (the underlying SentenceTransformer model is lazy-loaded and cached
# per process); never construct it inside a row-add loop. Nomic prefixes are
# NOT auto-applied by the registry, so embed_documents/embed_query prepend
# them manually.
_EMBEDDER = (
    get_registry()
    .get("sentence-transformers")
    .create(
        name=NOMIC_MODEL,
        device="cpu",
        trust_remote_code=True,
    )
)


class EmbeddingFunction(Protocol):
    def generate_embeddings(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]: ...


class LectureChunk(LanceModel):
    id: str
    video_id: str
    date: str
    title: str
    chunk_index: int
    start_seconds: float
    end_seconds: float
    text: str
    deep_link: str
    vector: Vector(EMBEDDING_DIMS)


def _embed_with_prefix(
    texts: list[str],
    prefix: str,
    embedder: EmbeddingFunction,
) -> list[list[float]]:
    prefixed = [prefix + text for text in texts]
    return [
        [float(value) for value in vector]
        for vector in embedder.generate_embeddings(prefixed)
    ]


def embed_documents(
    texts: list[str],
    embedder: EmbeddingFunction = _EMBEDDER,
) -> list[list[float]]:
    return _embed_with_prefix(texts, DOCUMENT_PREFIX, embedder)


def embed_query(
    text: str,
    embedder: EmbeddingFunction = _EMBEDDER,
) -> list[float]:
    return _embed_with_prefix([text], QUERY_PREFIX, embedder)[0]


def create_lectures_table(db: lancedb.DBConnection, name: str) -> lancedb.table.Table:
    return db.create_table(name, schema=LectureChunk, mode="overwrite")


class _StubEmbedder:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.seen: list[str] = []

    def generate_embeddings(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        self.seen.extend(texts)
        return [[float(i)] * EMBEDDING_DIMS for i, _ in enumerate(texts)]


def test_document_prefix_applied() -> None:
    stub = _StubEmbedder()
    vectors = embed_documents(["alpha", "beta"], embedder=stub)

    assert stub.seen == ["search_document: alpha", "search_document: beta"]
    assert len(vectors) == 2
    assert all(len(vector) == EMBEDDING_DIMS for vector in vectors)


def test_query_prefix_applied() -> None:
    stub = _StubEmbedder()
    vector = embed_query("what is a b-tree", embedder=stub)

    assert stub.seen == ["search_query: what is a b-tree"]
    assert len(vector) == EMBEDDING_DIMS


def test_schema_vector_is_fixed_size_float32_768() -> None:
    schema = LectureChunk.to_arrow_schema()
    vector_field = schema.field("vector")

    assert vector_field.type.list_size == EMBEDDING_DIMS
    assert str(vector_field.type.value_field.type) == "float"
    expected_columns = {
        "id",
        "video_id",
        "date",
        "title",
        "chunk_index",
        "start_seconds",
        "end_seconds",
        "text",
        "deep_link",
        "vector",
    }
    assert set(schema.names) == expected_columns


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_document_prefix_applied()
    test_query_prefix_applied()
    test_schema_vector_is_fixed_size_float32_768()

"""Fireworks hosted embeddings client: batching, retry with backoff, disk cache.

Swap-in for the local sentence-transformers embedder behind the same
EmbeddingFunction protocol as lecture_search.embed. The Nomic task prefixes
('search_document: ' / 'search_query: ') are NOT applied here — Fireworks
embeds input verbatim (docs/parity-gate.md), so callers must go through
lecture_search.embed.embed_documents / embed_query, which prepend the prefix
exactly once.

The disk cache is keyed by chunk id + text hash so a rerun over an unchanged
corpus makes zero API calls (cdgl-tds).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import tempfile
import time
from http import HTTPStatus
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import httpx

FIREWORKS_EMBEDDINGS_URL = "https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1/embeddings"
FIREWORKS_MODEL = "nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5"
EMBED_BATCH_SIZE = 64
MAX_RETRIES = 6
INITIAL_BACKOFF_SECONDS = 1.0
# Serverless list price for nomic-embed-text-v1.5 on Fireworks
# (https://fireworks.ai/pricing, serverless text-embedding tier).
COST_PER_MILLION_TOKENS_USD = 0.008

RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES = {408, 409, 425, 429}


def load_fireworks_api_key(env_file: Path) -> str:
    """Read FIREWORKS_API_KEY from a .env.local-style file. Never printed."""
    if not env_file.exists():
        msg = f"{env_file} not found"
        raise FileNotFoundError(msg)
    for raw_line in env_file.read_text().splitlines():
        line = raw_line.strip()
        if line.startswith("FIREWORKS_API_KEY=REDACTED
            return line.split("=", 1)[1].strip("\"'")
    msg = f"FIREWORKS_API_KEY not found in {env_file}"
    raise ValueError(msg)


def cache_key(chunk_id: str, text: str) -> str:
    """Cache key for a chunk: stable id plus a digest of the exact text."""
    digest = hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
    return f"{chunk_id}:{digest}"


class EmbeddingCache:
    """JSON-file cache: key -> 768-d float vector. Rewrite-on-save, atomic."""

    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        """Load (or lazily create) the cache file at `path`."""
        self.path = Path(path)
        self._vectors: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
        if self.path.exists():
            self._vectors = json.loads(self.path.read_text())

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """Number of cached vectors."""
        return len(self._vectors)

    def get(self, key: str) -> list[float] | None:
        """Return the cached vector for `key`, or None on a miss."""
        return self._vectors.get(key)

    def set(self, key: str, vector: list[float]) -> None:
        """Store `vector` under `key` (in memory until save())."""
        self._vectors[key] = vector

    def save(self) -> None:
        """Persist atomically: write a temp file, then replace."""
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
            dir=str(self.path.parent),
            prefix=self.path.name,
            suffix=".tmp",
        )
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as tmp:
            json.dump(self._vectors, tmp)
        Path(tmp_name).replace(self.path)


class FireworksEmbedder:
    """Batched Fireworks embeddings with retry/backoff on 429/5xx.

    Counters `requests_made` and `tokens_used` let the loader report measured
    cost and prove idempotent reruns make zero API calls.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        api_key: str,
        *,
        batch_size: int = EMBED_BATCH_SIZE,
        max_retries: int = MAX_RETRIES,
        timeout_seconds: float = 120.0,
        client: httpx.Client | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Create an embedder; pass `client` to inject a mock transport."""
        if batch_size < 1:
            msg = "batch_size must be >= 1"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        self._api_key = REDACTED
        self.batch_size = batch_size
        self.max_retries = max_retries
        self._client = client or httpx.Client(timeout=timeout_seconds)
        self.requests_made = 0
        self.tokens_used = 0

    def generate_embeddings(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        """Embed `texts` verbatim (no prefix), batching and retrying."""
        vectors: list[list[float]] = []
        for start in range(0, len(texts), self.batch_size):
            batch = texts[start : start + self.batch_size]
            payload = self._post_with_retry(batch)
            by_index = sorted(payload["data"], key=lambda item: item["index"])
            vectors.extend([float(v) for v in item["embedding"]] for item in by_index)
        return vectors

    def _post_with_retry(self, batch: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        delay = INITIAL_BACKOFF_SECONDS
        for attempt in range(self.max_retries):
            try:
                response = self._client.post(
                    FIREWORKS_EMBEDDINGS_URL,
                    headers={
                        "Authorization": f"Bearer {self._api_key}",
                        "Content-Type": "application/json",
                    },
                    json={"model": FIREWORKS_MODEL, "input": batch},
                )
            except httpx.TransportError:
                if attempt == self.max_retries - 1:
                    raise
                time.sleep(delay)
                delay *= 2
                continue

            if response.status_code < HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST:
                payload = response.json()
                self.requests_made += 1
                usage = payload.get("usage") or {}
                self.tokens_used += int(usage.get("total_tokens", 0))
                return payload

            retryable = (
                response.status_code in RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES
                or response.status_code >= HTTPStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
            )
            if not retryable or attempt == self.max_retries - 1:
                # Never include the request headers (they carry the API key).
                msg = (
                    f"Fireworks embeddings failed: HTTP {response.status_code} "
                    f"after {attempt + 1} attempt(s)"
                )
                raise RuntimeError(msg)
            retry_after = response.headers.get("Retry-After")
            wait = float(retry_after) if retry_after else delay
            time.sleep(wait)
            delay *= 2

        msg = "unreachable"  # pragma: no cover - loop always returns or raises
        raise RuntimeError(msg)

def _mock_transport(
    status_sequence: list[int],
) -> tuple[httpx.MockTransport, list[list[str]]]:
    """Transport returning the given statuses; final entry is a 200 payload."""
    seen_inputs: list[list[str]] = []

    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        body = json.loads(request.content)
        seen_inputs.append(body["input"])
        status = status_sequence[min(len(seen_inputs) - 1, len(status_sequence) - 1)]
        if status != 200:
            return httpx.Response(status)
        vectors = [
            {"index": i, "embedding": [float(i)] * 3}
            for i, _ in enumerate(body["input"])
        ]
        return httpx.Response(
            200,
            json={"data": vectors, "usage": {"total_tokens": 7 * len(body["input"])}},
        )

    return httpx.MockTransport(handler), seen_inputs


def test_cache_key_tracks_text() -> None:
    assert cache_key("vid:0", "alpha") == cache_key("vid:0", "alpha")
    assert cache_key("vid:0", "alpha") != cache_key("vid:0", "beta")
    assert cache_key("vid:0", "alpha") != cache_key("vid:1", "alpha")
    assert cache_key("vid:0", "alpha").startswith("vid:0:")


def test_embedding_cache_roundtrip(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    cache = EmbeddingCache(tmp_path / "cache.json")
    assert cache.get("k") is None
    cache.set("k", [1.0, 2.0])
    cache.save()

    reloaded = EmbeddingCache(tmp_path / "cache.json")
    assert len(reloaded) == 1
    assert reloaded.get("k") == [1.0, 2.0]


def test_batches_and_token_accounting() -> None:
    transport, seen = _mock_transport([200])
    embedder = FireworksEmbedder(
        "key",
        batch_size=2,
        client=httpx.Client(transport=transport),
    )
    vectors = embedder.generate_embeddings(["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"])

    assert seen == [["a", "b"], ["c", "d"], ["e"]]
    assert len(vectors) == 5
    assert embedder.requests_made == 3
    assert embedder.tokens_used == 7 * 5


def test_retry_on_429_then_success(monkeypatch) -> None:
    transport, seen = _mock_transport([429, 200])
    monkeypatch.setattr(time, "sleep", lambda _: None)
    embedder = FireworksEmbedder(
        "key",
        batch_size=64,
        client=httpx.Client(transport=transport),
    )
    vectors = embedder.generate_embeddings(["x"])

    assert len(seen) == 2  # one 429, one 200
    assert len(vectors) == 1
    assert embedder.requests_made == 1


def test_retry_on_5xx_exhaustion_raises(monkeypatch) -> None:
    transport, _ = _mock_transport([500])
    monkeypatch.setattr(time, "sleep", lambda _: None)
    embedder = FireworksEmbedder(
        "key",
        batch_size=64,
        max_retries=2,
        client=httpx.Client(transport=transport),
    )
    try:
        embedder.generate_embeddings(["x"])
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        assert "HTTP 500" in str(exc)
        assert "key" not in str(exc)  # never leak the API key
    else:
        raise AssertionError("expected RuntimeError")


def test_non_retryable_400_raises_immediately() -> None:
    transport, seen = _mock_transport([400])
    embedder = FireworksEmbedder(
        "key",
        batch_size=64,
        client=httpx.Client(transport=transport),
    )
    try:
        embedder.generate_embeddings(["x"])
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        assert "HTTP 400" in str(exc)
    else:
        raise AssertionError("expected RuntimeError")
    assert len(seen) == 1  # no retry on 4xx other than 429/408/409/425


if __name__ == "__main__":
    pass

"""Guard: the Nomic task prefix is added client-side, exactly once.

Fireworks embeds input verbatim (see docs/parity-gate.md), so any embedder
we swap in behaves like this verbatim stub: whatever embed_documents /
embed_query hand it is what gets embedded. Omitting the prefix drops cosine
to the stored vectors to ~0.93; doubling it is also wrong.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from lecture_search.embed import (
    DOCUMENT_PREFIX,
    EMBEDDING_DIMS,
    QUERY_PREFIX,
    embed_documents,
    embed_query,
)


class _VerbatimEmbedder:
    """Records exactly what would be sent to a no-prefix endpoint like Fireworks."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.sent: list[str] = []

    def generate_embeddings(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        self.sent.extend(texts)
        return [[0.0] * EMBEDDING_DIMS for _ in texts]


def test_documents_are_prefixed_exactly_once():
    embedder = _VerbatimEmbedder()
    embed_documents(["hash joins", "MVCC"], embedder=embedder)

    assert len(embedder.sent) == 2
    for sent, raw in zip(embedder.sent, ["hash joins", "MVCC"], strict=True):
        assert sent == DOCUMENT_PREFIX + raw
        assert sent.count(DOCUMENT_PREFIX) == 1


def test_query_is_prefixed_exactly_once():
    embedder = _VerbatimEmbedder()
    embed_query("what is a b-tree", embedder=embedder)

    assert embedder.sent == [QUERY_PREFIX + "what is a b-tree"]
    assert embedder.sent[0].count(QUERY_PREFIX) == 1


def test_document_and_query_prefixes_differ():
    assert DOCUMENT_PREFIX != QUERY_PREFIX

The endpoint is public and unauthenticated, so the tests that matter most
are the rejection cases: oversized or wrongly typed inputs, malformed query
vectors (wrong length, NaN/inf, non-numbers), oversized request bodies,
SQL-injection shaped video IDs, and proof that nothing user-controlled is
ever interpolated into a WHERE clause, and no vectors/keys leave in a
response. Runs fully offline with fake table doubles — no Modal, no network.
"""

)

        "date_from": None,
        "date_to": None,

    }
    base.update(overrides)

# Reflex architecture: web.web -> web.pages.index -> web.components.* (public exports only).

# https://docs.gauge.sh/usage/configuration
source_roots = ["."]
root_module = "forbid"
exact = true
forbid_circular_dependencies = true
ignore_type_checking_imports = false
include_string_imports = true
# Three layers with strict ordering: production entrypoints -> pages ->
# components. Layers are NOT closed (the closed-layer flag does not
# allow per-module exemptions, and the smoke net in `tests/` needs to
# construct status_card directly with literal inputs to keep regression
# coverage honest). The intended `web.web -> web.pages.* ->
# web.components.*` flow is still enforced at the visible-edges:

class EmbeddingFunction(BaseModel, ABC):
    """
    An ABC for embedding functions.

    All concrete embedding functions must implement the following methods:
    1. compute_query_embeddings() which takes a query and returns a list of embeddings
    2. compute_source_embeddings() which returns a list of embeddings for
       the source column
    For text data, the two will be the same. For multi-modal data, the source column
    might be images and the vector column might be text.
    3. ndims() which returns the number of dimensions of the vector column

    max_retries: int = (

    )
    _ndims: int = PrivateAttr()
    _original_args: dict = PrivateAttr()

    @classmethod
    def create(cls, **kwargs):
        """
        Create an instance of the embedding function
        """
        resolved_kwargs = cls.__resolveVariables(kwargs)
        instance = cls(**resolved_kwargs)
        instance._original_args = kwargs
        return instance

    @classmethod
    def __resolveVariables(cls, args: dict) -> dict:
        """
        Resolve variables in the args
        """
        from .registry import EmbeddingFunctionRegistry

        new_args = copy.deepcopy(args)

        registry = EmbeddingFunctionRegistry.get_instance()
        sensitive_keys = cls.sensitive_keys()
        for k, v in new_args.items():
            if isinstance(v, str) and not v.startswith("$var:") and k in sensitive_keys:

                    f"Sensitive key '{k}' cannot be set to a hardcoded value"
                )

"""Chunk lecture transcripts into overlapping, deep-linkable windows.

Transcripts are YouTube auto-captions stored as
``<date>·<video_id>·transcription.json`` files. Each lecture becomes a
sequence of ``ChunkRecord`` windows (default 75 s with 15 s overlap) whose
metadata — video_id, date, title, deep link — comes from a per-directory
``titles.json`` (sample corpus) or the full-corpus ``metadata/titles_all.json``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TypedDict, cast


@dataclass
class Segment:
    """One transcript segment: a timed span of caption text."""

    start: float
    end: float
    text: str


@dataclass
class ChunkRecord:
    """One chunk window over a lecture, with deep link back to the video."""

    id: str
    video_id: str
    date: str
    title: str
    chunk_index: int
    start_seconds: float
    end_seconds: float
    text: str
    deep_link: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChunkContext:
    """Lecture identity stamped onto every chunk the transcript yields."""

    video_id: str
    date: str
    title: str


class TranscriptSegment(TypedDict):
    """One segment entry in a ``*·transcription.json`` file."""

    start: float
    end: float
    text: str


class Transcript(TypedDict, total=False):
    """Parsed ``*·transcription.json`` payload."""

    segments: list[TranscriptSegment]


class TitleMeta(TypedDict, total=False):
    """One entry of a titles mapping: per-lecture metadata."""

    date: str
    title: str
    duration: float


def chunk_transcript(
    segments: list[Segment],
    context: ChunkContext,
    window_duration: float = 75.0,
    overlap_duration: float = 15.0,
) -> list[ChunkRecord]:
    """Split one lecture's segments into overlapping chunk windows.

    A new chunk starts whenever the accumulated window would exceed
    ``window_duration`` seconds; the next window rewinds by
    ``overlap_duration`` seconds (bounded by the lecture start) so
    sentences spanning a boundary appear in both chunks.
    """
    if not segments:
        return []

    video_id = context.video_id
    chunk_index = 0
    chunks: list[ChunkRecord] = []
    current_start = segments[0].start
    current_text_parts: list[str] = []
    current_start_time = segments[0].start

    for segment in segments:
        if segment.end - current_start > window_duration:
            if current_text_parts:
                chunk_text = " ".join(current_text_parts)
                chunk_end = segment.start
                chunks.append(
                    ChunkRecord(
                        id=f"{video_id}:{chunk_index}",
                        video_id=video_id,
                        date=context.date,
                        title=context.title,
                        chunk_index=chunk_index,
                        start_seconds=current_start_time,
                        end_seconds=chunk_end,
                        text=chunk_text,
                        deep_link=f"https://youtu.be/{video_id}?t={int(current_start_time)}",
                    ),
                )
                chunk_index += 1

            current_start_time = max(
                current_start - overlap_duration,
                segments[0].start,
            )
            current_text_parts = []
            current_start = segment.start

        current_text_parts.append(segment.text)

    if current_text_parts:
        chunk_text = " ".join(current_text_parts)
        chunk_end = segments[-1].end
        chunks.append(
            ChunkRecord(
                id=f"{video_id}:{chunk_index}",
                video_id=video_id,
                date=context.date,
                title=context.title,
                chunk_index=chunk_index,
                start_seconds=current_start_time,
                end_seconds=chunk_end,
                text=chunk_text,
                deep_link=f"https://youtu.be/{video_id}?t={int(current_start_time)}",
            ),
        )

    return chunks


def load_transcript(transcript_path: Path) -> Transcript:
    """Parse one ``*·transcription.json`` file."""
    return cast("Transcript", json.loads(transcript_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))


def load_titles(sample_dir: Path) -> dict[str, TitleMeta]:
    """Load video_id -> {date, title, duration} metadata from titles.json."""
    titles_path = sample_dir / "titles.json"
    if not titles_path.exists():
        return {}
    return cast(
        "dict[str, TitleMeta]",
        json.loads(titles_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
    )


def load_titles_all(metadata_path: Path) -> dict[str, TitleMeta]:
    """Load video_id -> {date, title, duration} for the full 595-lecture corpus."""
    return cast(
        "dict[str, TitleMeta]",
        json.loads(Path(metadata_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
    )


def process_corpus_transcripts(
    transcripts_dir: Path,
    titles: dict[str, TitleMeta],
    limit: int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, list[ChunkRecord]]:
    """Chunk a directory of full-corpus transcripts.

    Like process_sample_transcripts, but titles/dates come from the
    metadata/titles_all.json mapping (passed in) instead of a per-directory
    titles.json. Filename date is the fallback when a video_id is missing
    from the metadata. `limit` caps the number of transcripts processed
    (sorted order) for partial runs.
    """
    results: dict[str, list[ChunkRecord]] = {}
    transcript_files = sorted(transcripts_dir.glob("*·transcription.json"))
    if limit is not None:
        transcript_files = transcript_files[:limit]

    for transcript_file in transcript_files:
        date_from_name, video_id, _ = transcript_file.name.split("·", 2)
        data = load_transcript(transcript_file)

        meta = titles.get(video_id, {})
        title = meta.get("title", "")
        date = meta.get("date", date_from_name)

        segments = [
            Segment(start=seg["start"], end=seg["end"], text=seg["text"])
            for seg in data.get("segments", [])
        ]

        chunks = chunk_transcript(
            segments=segments,
            context=ChunkContext(video_id=video_id, date=date, title=title),
        )
        results[video_id] = chunks

    return results


def process_sample_transcripts(
    sample_dir: Path,
) -> dict[str, list[ChunkRecord]]:
    """Chunk a sample directory, reading titles from its titles.json."""
    results: dict[str, list[ChunkRecord]] = {}
    titles = load_titles(sample_dir)

    for transcript_file in sorted(sample_dir.glob("*·transcription.json")):
        filename = transcript_file.name
        date, video_id, _ = filename.split("·", 2)

        data = load_transcript(transcript_file)

        title = titles.get(video_id, {}).get("title", "")

        segments = [
            Segment(start=seg["start"], end=seg["end"], text=seg["text"])
            for seg in data.get("segments", [])
        ]

        chunks = chunk_transcript(
            segments=segments,
            context=ChunkContext(video_id=video_id, date=date, title=title),
        )
        results[video_id] = chunks

    return results

"""Client-side Nomic v1.5 embeddings and the LanceDB lectures table schema.

Embedding is client-side by design: callers embed with
``embed_documents``/``embed_query`` (which prepend the Nomic task prefixes
exactly once) and send vectors to the search API — the Modal container
never runs a model. ``LectureChunk`` is the LanceDB table schema; the
vector column is a fixed-size 768-d float32 list.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Protocol, cast

from lancedb.embeddings import EmbeddingFunction as _LanceEmbeddingFunction
from lancedb.embeddings import get_registry
# Vector(dim) builds a pyarrow-backed type dynamically — the canonical
# lancedb schema idiom; its value_type parameter is untyped upstream.
from lancedb.pydantic import (  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownVariableType]
    LanceModel,
    Vector,
)

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    import lancedb

NOMIC_MODEL = "nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5"
EMBEDDING_DIMS = 768
DOCUMENT_PREFIX = "search_document: "
QUERY_PREFIX = "search_query: "


class EmbeddingFunction(Protocol):
    """The slice of an embedding backend this module depends on."""

    def generate_embeddings(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        """Embed each text into one fixed-dimension vector."""
        ...


class _RegistryEmbedder:
    """Adapt a lancedb registry embedder to the local EmbeddingFunction.

    lancedb's ``EmbeddingFunction.generate_embeddings`` is typed as
    returning ``list[np.ndarray | None]``; this adapter normalizes to plain
    float lists so embed_documents/embed_query stay backend-agnostic.
    """

    def __init__(self, inner: _LanceEmbeddingFunction) -> None:
        self._inner = inner

    def generate_embeddings(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        """Embed texts via the wrapped lancedb embedder."""
        embeddings: list[list[float]] = []
        for vector in self._inner.generate_embeddings(texts):
            if vector is None:
                msg = "embedder returned no vector for a text"
                raise RuntimeError(msg)
            values = cast("list[float]", vector)
            embeddings.append([float(value) for value in values])
        return embeddings


def _create_registry_embedder() -> EmbeddingFunction:
    """Instantiate the Nomic v1.5 sentence-transformers embedder.

    Instantiating is cheap (the underlying SentenceTransformer model is
    lazy-loaded and cached per process); never construct it inside a
    row-add loop.
    """
    embedder_cls = get_registry().get("sentence-transformers")
    # lancedb's EmbeddingFunction.create(**kwargs) is untyped upstream.
    create = embedder_cls.create  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]
    inner = create(
        name=NOMIC_MODEL,
        device="cpu",
        trust_remote_code=True,
    )
    return _RegistryEmbedder(inner)


# Registry embedder instantiated ONCE at module import (see
# _create_registry_embedder). Nomic prefixes are NOT auto-applied by the
# registry, so embed_documents/embed_query prepend them manually.
_EMBEDDER: EmbeddingFunction = _create_registry_embedder()


class LectureChunk(LanceModel):
    """LanceDB schema for one chunk row (vector is 768-d float32)."""

    id: str
    video_id: str
    date: str
    title: str
    chunk_index: int
    start_seconds: float
    end_seconds: float
    text: str
    deep_link: str
    # Vector(dim) constructs the column type at call time; there is no
    # static type form for it (dynamic lancedb/pyarrow API).
    # pyrefly: ignore[invalid-annotation]
    vector: Vector(EMBEDDING_DIMS)  # pyright: ignore[reportInvalidTypeForm]


def _embed_with_prefix(
    texts: list[str],
    prefix: str,
    embedder: EmbeddingFunction,
) -> list[list[float]]:
    prefixed = [prefix + text for text in texts]
    return [
        [float(value) for value in vector]
        for vector in embedder.generate_embeddings(prefixed)
    ]


def embed_documents(
    texts: list[str],
    embedder: EmbeddingFunction = _EMBEDDER,
) -> list[list[float]]:
    """Embed corpus documents with the Nomic ``search_document: `` prefix."""
    return _embed_with_prefix(texts, DOCUMENT_PREFIX, embedder)


def embed_query(
    text: str,
    embedder: EmbeddingFunction = _EMBEDDER,
) -> list[float]:
    """Embed one query with the Nomic ``search_query: `` prefix."""
    return _embed_with_prefix([text], QUERY_PREFIX, embedder)[0]


def create_lectures_table(db: lancedb.DBConnection, name: str) -> lancedb.table.Table:
    """Create (overwriting) the lectures table with the LectureChunk schema."""
    # lancedb's create_table(data=...) parameter is untyped upstream; this
    # call passes only schema=.
    return db.create_table(  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]
        name,
        schema=LectureChunk,
        mode="overwrite",
    )

"""Guards for lecture_search.embed: prefix application and table schema.

The stub embedder records exactly what it is handed, proving the Nomic task
prefixes are prepended exactly once; the schema guard pins the vector column
to a fixed-size 768-d float32 list (the Nomic v1.5 embedding shape).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from lecture_search.embed import (
    EMBEDDING_DIMS,
    LectureChunk,
    embed_documents,
    embed_query,
)


class _StubEmbedder:
    """Verbatim embedder double: records inputs, returns index-filled vectors."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.seen: list[str] = []

    def generate_embeddings(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        self.seen.extend(texts)
        return [[float(i)] * EMBEDDING_DIMS for i, _ in enumerate(texts)]


def test_document_prefix_applied() -> None:
    texts = ["alpha", "beta"]
    stub = _StubEmbedder()
    vectors = embed_documents(texts, embedder=stub)

    assert stub.seen == ["search_document: alpha", "search_document: beta"]
    assert len(vectors) == len(texts)
    assert all(len(vector) == EMBEDDING_DIMS for vector in vectors)


def test_query_prefix_applied() -> None:
    stub = _StubEmbedder()
    vector = embed_query("what is a b-tree", embedder=stub)

    assert stub.seen == ["search_query: what is a b-tree"]
    assert len(vector) == EMBEDDING_DIMS


def test_schema_vector_is_fixed_size_float32_768() -> None:
    schema = LectureChunk.to_arrow_schema()
    vector_field = schema.field("vector")

    assert vector_field.type.list_size == EMBEDDING_DIMS
    assert str(vector_field.type.value_field.type) == "float"
    expected_columns = {
        "id",
        "video_id",
        "date",
        "title",
        "chunk_index",
        "start_seconds",
        "end_seconds",
        "text",
        "deep_link",
        "vector",
    }
    assert set(schema.names) == expected_columns

"""Guards for lecture_search.fireworks: cache, batching, retry/backoff.

Runs fully offline against an httpx MockTransport. The retry tests also pin
the security posture: the API key must never appear in raised errors.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from http import HTTPStatus
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
import pytest

from lecture_search.fireworks import EmbeddingCache, FireworksEmbedder, cache_key

MOCK_EMBEDDING_DIMS = 3
TOKENS_PER_INPUT_TEXT = 7
NON_RETRYABLE_STATUSES = {408, 409, 425, 429}


def _mock_transport(
    status_sequence: list[int],
) -> tuple[httpx.MockTransport, list[list[str]]]:
    """Transport returning the given statuses; final entry is a 200 payload."""
    seen_inputs: list[list[str]] = []

    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        body = json.loads(request.content)
        seen_inputs.append(body["input"])
        status = status_sequence[min(len(seen_inputs) - 1, len(status_sequence) - 1)]
        if status != HTTPStatus.OK:
            return httpx.Response(status)
        vectors = [
            {"index": i, "embedding": [float(i)] * MOCK_EMBEDDING_DIMS}
            for i, _ in enumerate(body["input"])
        ]
        return httpx.Response(
            HTTPStatus.OK,
            json={
                "data": vectors,
                "usage": {"total_tokens": TOKENS_PER_INPUT_TEXT * len(body["input"])},
            },
        )

    return httpx.MockTransport(handler), seen_inputs


def _embedder(transport: httpx.MockTransport, **overrides: object) -> FireworksEmbedder:
    kwargs: dict[str, object] = {
        "batch_size": 64,
        "client": httpx.Client(transport=transport),
    }
    kwargs.update(overrides)
    return FireworksEmbedder("key", **kwargs)  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def test_cache_key_tracks_text() -> None:
    assert cache_key("vid:0", "alpha") == cache_key("vid:0", "alpha")
    assert cache_key("vid:0", "alpha") != cache_key("vid:0", "beta")
    assert cache_key("vid:0", "alpha") != cache_key("vid:1", "alpha")
    assert cache_key("vid:0", "alpha").startswith("vid:0:")


def test_embedding_cache_roundtrip(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    cache = EmbeddingCache(tmp_path / "cache.json")
    assert cache.get("k") is None
    cache.set("k", [1.0, 2.0])
    cache.save()

    reloaded = EmbeddingCache(tmp_path / "cache.json")
    assert len(reloaded) == 1
    assert reloaded.get("k") == [1.0, 2.0]


def test_batches_and_token_accounting() -> None:
    transport, seen = _mock_transport([HTTPStatus.OK])
    texts = ["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"]
    embedder = FireworksEmbedder(
        "key",
        batch_size=2,
        client=httpx.Client(transport=transport),
    )
    vectors = embedder.generate_embeddings(texts)

    assert seen == [["a", "b"], ["c", "d"], ["e"]]
    assert len(vectors) == len(texts)
    assert embedder.requests_made == len(seen)
    assert embedder.tokens_used == TOKENS_PER_INPUT_TEXT * len(texts)


def test_retry_on_429_then_success(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    statuses = [HTTPStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, HTTPStatus.OK]
    transport, seen = _mock_transport(statuses)
    monkeypatch.setattr(time, "sleep", lambda _seconds: None)
    embedder = _embedder(transport)
    vectors = embedder.generate_embeddings(["x"])

    assert len(seen) == len(statuses)  # one 429, one 200
    assert len(vectors) == 1
    assert embedder.requests_made == 1


def test_retry_on_5xx_exhaustion_raises(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    transport, _ = _mock_transport([HTTPStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR])
    monkeypatch.setattr(time, "sleep", lambda _seconds: None)
    embedder = _embedder(transport, max_retries=2)

    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="HTTP 500") as exc_info:
        embedder.generate_embeddings(["x"])
    assert "key" not in str(exc_info.value)  # never leak the API key


def test_non_retryable_400_raises_immediately() -> None:
    transport, seen = _mock_transport([HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST])
    embedder = _embedder(transport)

    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="HTTP 400"):
        embedder.generate_embeddings(["x"])
    assert len(seen) == 1  # no retry on 4xx other than 408/409/425/429

# Trunk runs linters from a sandboxed tmp dir, so pyrefly's usual environment
    # discovery (interpreter resolution via PATH lookup) lands in Trunk's sandbox,
    # not the project workspace. The pyrefly plugin (oss-linter-trunk-pyrefly v0.2.0)
    # claims to pass --python-interpreter-path ${workspace}/.venv/bin/python and
    # --search-path ${workspace} automatically, but this fails in environments where
    # .venv/bin/python is a symlink to /usr/local/bin/python3 (typical in cloud
    # sandboxes), because pyrefly's interpreter-resolver follows the symlink target,
    # landing outside the venv's site-packages. See #120.
    #
    # This overrides the plugin's whole pyrefly invocation to explicitly pass the
    # workspace venv paths, matching the pattern used for pyright above. Re-check
    # this command against the plugin definition whenever trunk.yaml bumps plugin
    # versions.
    - name: pyrefly
      commands:
        - name: lint
          run: pyrefly check --python-interpreter-path ${workspace}/.venv/bin/python --search-path ${workspace} --output-format=min-text --summary=none ${target}
